en: The Chapter on Similes, Section on the Water-Jar.
1. The Question of the Jar’s Part “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘one part of a jar should be taken,’ which is that one part that should be taken?
“Just as, Great King, a jar that is full does not leak;”
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga who has reached perfection in the scriptures, realization, the teachings, and the state of a recluse, should not be boastful;
he should not give rise to conceit; he should not display arrogance. He should be one whose conceit is subdued and whose arrogance is humbled—upright, gentle, and free from self-aggrandizement.
This, Great King, is one quality of a water-jar that should be adopted.
And this was said, Great King, by the Blessed One, the God above gods, in the Sutta Nipāta:
“Whatever is hollow, that makes a sound.”
That which is full is indeed peaceful;
the fool is like a half-filled jar,
while the wise man is like a lake that is full.”
The first question concerning the pot-breaker.
